Reason for Admission: Mr. Steven Roman, a 52-year-old male, was admitted for routine follow-up and management of his prediabetes, as indicated by an A1c level of 5.5. The patient has been under our care for this condition since 2017.

Hospital Course: Mr. Roman's hospital course was uneventful. He was admitted for a scheduled visit to monitor his prediabetes, eczema, erectile dysfunction, and gout. Throughout his stay, he remained in stable condition with no acute changes in his chronic conditions. His A1c levels have been consistently around 5.6, with minor fluctuations noted at 5.7 in August 2024 and returning to 5.6 in subsequent tests.

The patient's eczema, erectile dysfunction, and gout were also evaluated. His eczema remains well-controlled with topical treatments. There were no acute flare-ups or complications noted. His erectile dysfunction continues to be managed effectively with sildenafil. Gout management with colchicine has been successful, with no reports of acute gout attacks during this admission or in recent history.

Procedures: No procedures were performed during this admission. The focus was on routine evaluation and medication management.

Discharge Medications:
1. Tacrolimus topical 0.1% - For eczema, apply as directed.
2. Triamcinolone topical 0.1% - For eczema, apply as directed.
3. Sildenafil 50 mg - For erectile dysfunction, take as needed, not more than once daily.
4. Colchicine 0.6 mg - For gout prophylaxis, take daily as directed.

Discharge Instructions: Mr. Roman was discharged home in stable condition. He was advised to continue with his current medication regimen and lifestyle modifications for prediabetes management, including diet and exercise. Follow-up appointments were scheduled to monitor his conditions and adjust treatment plans as necessary.

Follow-Up: Mr. Roman is to follow up with Dr. Jeffrey Murray at the Ashley-Short Clinic in three months for a routine check-up. He was encouraged to monitor his blood glucose levels at home and report any significant changes or symptoms.
